title: Verified TLS helper ownership and cleanup
summary: When socat is used as the TLS adapter, the transport owns an exact helper PID and verifies command-line ownership before signaling it. Close drops the loopback socket, attempts TERM, waits boundedly, then re-verifies ownership before KILL escalation.
invariants: Never signal a reused PID merely because the number matches.
Zombie/defunct helper state counts as network-resource release.
Top-level HALT cleanup must close the helper-backed transport.
Orderly terminal close propagates helper shutdown failure rather than hiding it.

provenance.claim: Supports this Terminal Machine/TN5250 continuity article.
